title: Historic barn near Grade I listed Hunts property could become five-bedroom home
content: Find, save and share Public Notices that affect you in the area. The Public Notice Portal carries statutory public notices published in local newspapers and is the fastest and most effective way of finding out what is happening in YOUR neighbourhood. Plans have been submitted to turn a historic outbuilding beside a Grade I listed building into a five-bedroom home. Mick Hilless has applied to Huntingdonshire District Council to turn a barn and office building linked to Bodsey House into a home on Bodsey Toll Road, Ramsey. Bodsey House is Grade I listed, meaning it is of exceptional interest. The property was once a 13th-century hermitage belonging to Ramsey Abbey but has since been altered and turned into a family home. The plans would turn the barn and office building at the rear of the site into one five-bedroom home. The historic barn is curtilage listed, which means it is legally protected as it sits within the grounds of a listed building. Documents by Scroxton Architects say the barn and office building are dilapidated and no longer suitable for modern agricultural or commercial use. title: Jail for uninsured driver who fled Cambs crash scene after killing pedestrian
content: A uninsured driver from Cambridgeshire who fled the scene after hitting and killing a pedestrian has been jailed. Marcin Pilarski, 36, struck Sam Pope, 28, as he walked alongside Oil Mills Road, Ramsey Mereside, at just before 11pm on May 11, 2024. The crash was only reported when another driver called 999 after seeing Mr Pope, of Lincoln Road, Peterborough, laying in the road. Emergency services attended but despite their efforts, Mr Pope was declared dead at the scene. In a tribute, his family said: "Sam was a free spirit, who liked to live his life at 100mph and believed that rules were meant to be broken. "We shall miss his smile and crazy sense of humour that would always make you laugh, despite what mood you were in that day. "Sam was a rough diamond with a heart made of gold and will leave a big hole in our lives." Sam Pope was struck as he walked alongside Oil Mills Road (Image: Cambridgeshire Police) Less than an hour after the collision, at 11.40pm, police were called by Pilarski’s partner who told them he had returned home in her Vauxhall Astra. title: New 20-year Hunts parking plan set for debate as demand set to rise
content: Huntingdonshire District Council's cabinet is set to discuss a new 20-year parking strategy aimed at supporting town centres, improving customer experience and planning for future growth. Huntingdonshire District Council’s cabinet will consider the proposed plan when it meets today (Tuesday September 15). Work on the new parking strategy began in early October 2025 after a procurement exercise. The strategy will run from 2026 to 2046 and focus on economic growth, customer service and future demand.
